sectionToMerge.h2: Frequently Asked Questions About NGS Testing Cost Worldwide
sectionToMerge.intro: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) testing prices vary widely between countries, laboratories, and panel sizes. These answers explain what drives the cost and what international patients should check before ordering a test.

groups.title: Understanding NGS Testing and Its Cost

items.q: What is NGS testing and why does it cost more than routine tests?
items.a: NGS (next-generation sequencing) is a genomic test that reads many cancer-related genes at once to guide precision oncology decisions. It generally costs more than single-gene tests because it uses advanced sequencing machines, specialised reagents, bioinformatics analysis, and expert interpretation. The price depends on how many genes are tested, the laboratory, and the country. Final cost and clinical value should be discussed with a qualified oncology team based on the specific cancer type.

items.q: How much does NGS testing cost worldwide?
items.a: NGS testing worldwide can range from roughly a few hundred to several thousand US dollars, depending on the panel and laboratory. Smaller targeted panels are usually cheaper, while large comprehensive genomic profiling of hundreds of genes costs more. Prices differ across the US, Europe, India, and other regions. These figures are estimates only, and the actual cost depends on the lab, sample type, and tests advised by the treating team.

items.q: Why does NGS testing cost differ so much between countries?
items.a: NGS cost varies between countries because of differences in laboratory infrastructure, reagent import prices, currency, labour, and local competition. Testing done in the US or Western Europe is often more expensive than equivalent panels processed in India or parts of Asia. Sample shipping abroad can also add cost. Because pricing and turnaround differ, patients should compare accredited laboratories and confirm details with their oncology team before choosing where to test.

groups.title: What Affects the Price of an NGS Test

items.q: What factors affect the final cost of an NGS test?
items.a: The final cost of an NGS test depends mainly on panel size, sample type, laboratory, and country. Larger panels covering more genes, RNA fusion analysis, or liquid biopsy from blood generally cost more than small tumour-tissue panels. Additional charges may include biopsy, sample preparation, shipping, and report interpretation. Because these variables differ for each patient, the treating oncology team can advise which panel is clinically appropriate and cost-effective.

items.q: Is a tissue NGS test cheaper than a liquid biopsy?
items.a: Tissue-based NGS is often less expensive than a liquid biopsy, but this is not always the case. Liquid biopsy analyses tumour DNA from a blood sample and may cost more due to the technology involved, though it avoids a surgical biopsy. The right option depends on cancer type, tumour availability, and clinical need. A qualified oncology team should decide which test is suitable, as cost is only one of several factors.

items.q: Does a larger gene panel always cost more?
items.a: Larger gene panels usually cost more because they sequence and analyse more genes, but a bigger panel is not always better for every patient. Comprehensive genomic profiling may be valuable in advanced or rare cancers, while a focused panel can be enough in other situations. The clinical benefit depends on cancer type, stage, and treatment goals. The treating oncology team should decide which panel size is appropriate before ordering the test.

items.q: Does insurance cover the cost of NGS testing?
items.a: Insurance coverage for NGS testing varies widely by country, insurer, and clinical indication. Some plans cover comprehensive genomic profiling for specific advanced cancers, while others cover only limited testing or none at all. Approval may require documentation of cancer type and medical necessity. Patients should confirm coverage, co-payments, and pre-authorisation rules with their insurer and treating team, as out-of-pocket cost can differ significantly between individuals.

items.q: How does CancerFax help patients with NGS testing cost worldwide?
items.a: CancerFax helps patients organize medical reports, identify accredited laboratories or specialists offering NGS testing, estimate possible costs across regions, and coordinate second opinions, sample logistics, and follow-up support. Testing and treatment decisions are always made by the qualified oncology team after reviewing the patient's diagnosis, stage, biomarkers, previous treatment, and overall health. CancerFax does not guarantee specific pricing, laboratory acceptance, or test outcomes.
